title: Processing fallopian tube tissue for single cell sequencing analysis
author: Ramlogan Sowamber
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bu4znyx6

steps.title: Mince Fallopian Tube Tissue
steps.instruction: Process the fallopian tube and fimbria tissue samples collected within two hours of removal (transported in DMEM with 10% FBS on ice).

substeps.instruction: In a biological safety cabinet with appropriate PPE, aspirate the transport medium, leaving behind 5 mL of media.
Place tissue into a cell culture dish and finely mince using a blade (do not use a mortar and pestle).
Label a 50 mL conical tube with identifying information.
Transfer minced tissue to the 50 mL conical tube using a 25 mL pipette.

steps.title: Digest Tissue with Pronase
steps.instruction: Perform enzymatic digestion of the minced tissue.

substeps.instruction: Add 15 mL of pronase solution and 150 uL of DNase to the 50 mL tube.
Place the tube on an orbital shaker at 4 °C for a minimum of 24 hours and a maximum of 72 hours.

steps.title: Wash and Collect Cells
steps.instruction: Stop the digestion and isolate the cells.

substeps.instruction: Remove the 50 mL tube from the 4 °C shaker.
Add approximately 20 mL of RPMI solution to the tube (total volume should not exceed 40 mL).
Gently shake the 50 mL tube back and forth to mix.
Place the tube in a rack and allow the tissue to settle to the bottom.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1500 rpm for 15 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Store or Process Cells
steps.instruction: Decide whether to cryopreserve the cells or proceed to immediate processing.

substeps.instruction: To cryopreserve: Carefully remove the supernatant, re-suspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of freezing media, and store in a -80 °C freezer (transfer to liquid nitrogen within 48 hours).
To process immediately: Gently aspirate the supernatant and proceed to the cell suspension steps.

steps.title: Process Fresh Cell Pellets
steps.instruction: Prepare cells from a fresh pellet in a 15 mL conical tube for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Gently re-suspend the pellet with 500 uL of cell culture media to dissociate the pellet.
Pre-wet a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube with a cell strainer cap using 50 uL of cell culture media.
Ensure liquid flows through the cap by gravity; if it does not, pipette the liquid up and down or seal with parafilm and centrifuge at 300 x g for 1 min.
Add the 500 uL of resuspended cells to the pre-wetted cell strainer cap and allow cells to flow through by gravity into the 5 mL tube.
Place parafilm on the cap to prevent contamination when removing from the biological safety cabinet.

steps.title: Process Frozen Cell Pellets
steps.instruction: Thaw and prepare cells previously frozen at -80 °C or in liquid nitrogen.

substeps.instruction: Thaw the cryo-vial rapidly into 5 mL of pre-warmed cell culture USG media.
Centrifuge cells at 300 x g for 5 minutes.
Gently re-suspend cells in 500 uL of cell culture media.
Pre-wet a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube with a cell strainer cap using 50 uL of cell culture media.
Ensure liquid flows through the cap by gravity; if it does not, pipette the liquid up and down or seal with parafilm and centrifuge at 300 x g for 1 min.
Add the 500 uL of resuspended cells to the pre-wetted cell strainer cap and allow cells to flow through by gravity into the 5 mL tube.
Place parafilm on the cap to prevent contamination when removing from the biological safety cabinet.

steps.title: Incubate and Assess Viability
steps.instruction: Prepare cells for sequencing and verify quality.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes with cells in an incubator (37 °C and 5% CO2) for 15 minutes.
Count cells using the Nexcelom Cellometer K2 or an equivalent cell counter.
Assess viability and cell numbers before proceeding to sequencing.

steps.title: Culture Remaining Cells
steps.instruction: If cell samples remain after sequencing, culture them in a Primaria plate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 24-well Primaria plate by coating wells with 250 uL of collagen.
Add 250 uL of cell culture media to each well.
Remove cells from the incubator (from the 15-minute step) and very gently re-suspend the liquid.
Add cells to a labeled well of the collagen-coated Primaria plate using a pipette.
Gently move the plate back and forth to evenly distribute cells.
Place the plate in an incubator (37 °C and 5% CO2) to allow primary fallopian tube cells to grow.
